chapters.intro: Black mirrors you with ...Bc5. You answer with c3 and d3, castle, and put a rook on e1. Then you either push d4 or bring the queen's knight to g3 via d2 and f1. The ideas carry over from game to game, so you'll recognise these positions quickly.

chapters.title: Second-move alternatives
chapters.intro: Some opponents don't play 2...Nc6. You'll learn a sensible line against the Philidor (2...d6), the Petrov (2...Nf6) and the risky Latvian Gambit (2...f5).

chapters.title: Against 1...Nf6 and King's Indian setups
chapters.intro: After 1...Nf6 you keep the same setup. Against ...g6 and ...Bg7 put your bishop on e2 and play h3, so the f4 bishop can retreat to h2 and survive ...Nh5 and ...e5. Against an early ...c5 with ...Qb6, know your one sharp answer.

courses.name: London System
courses.tagline: One setup against everything. Bf4, e3, c3, Nf3, Nbd2, Bd3, and go.
courses.description: The London is the easiest repertoire in chess to learn: you put your pieces on the same squares in almost every game. This course teaches the setup, the key plans (Ne5 with f4, or the e4 break), and the exact moves you need against Black's sharpest tries: ...c5 with ...Qb6, early ...Bf5 and ...Bg4, and King's Indian setups.

chapters.title: Offbeat defences and traps
chapters.intro: The Albin, Chigorin and Baltic try to catch you unprepared. Learn the one sensible setup against each, and the Lasker Trap in the Albin.

courses.name: Queen's Gambit

chapters.title: Two Knights, Fantasy and other tries

chapters.title: Exchange Variation: 3.exd5
chapters.intro: The Exchange is symmetrical, but it's not a draw if you play actively. Develop with ...Bd6, ...Nc6 and ...Nge7, pin with ...Bg4, and think about castling long.

chapters.title: Tarrasch: 3.Nd2
chapters.intro: White's knight goes to d2 so it can't be pinned. You reply 3...c5, and after exd5 you recapture with the queen. Black gets free development and White gets a slight lead in time. It's a solid, well-tested line.

chapters.title: Classical: 3.Nc3 Nf6
chapters.intro: Against 3.Nc3 you develop with 3...Nf6 and put pressure on e4. If White plays 4.e5 the knight drops to d7 and you hit the centre with ...c5 and ...f6. If White pins with 4.Bg5, unpin with ...Be7.

wrong: 3...f6: hit the head of the chain
quizzes.question: White played 3.e5. What's the French's key counter?
quizzes.answer: 3...c5: hit the base of the pawn chain on d4
quizzes.explanation: Attack a pawn chain at its base. ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 all pile up on d4.

quizzes.question: You've won the d4 pawn. Why play 10...a6?
quizzes.answer: It stops Nb5, which would hit c7 and d6
quizzes.explanation: In the Milner-Barry, White's knight wants to jump to b5. ...a6 takes away that square so you can develop calmly with the extra pawn.

wrong: Because the queen can't be attacked on d5
Because White has to recapture on d4 first
quizzes.question: Why is 4...Qxd5 safe in the Tarrasch?
quizzes.answer: White's knight is on d2, not c3, so it can't gain a tempo on the queen
quizzes.explanation: 3.Nd2 blocks the queen's knight from c3. The queen is stable on d5 for a move and then drops back to d6.

quizzes.question: White played 5.f4 to support e5. What's your plan?
quizzes.answer: Hit d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 or ...Bc5
quizzes.explanation: The d4 pawn holds White's chain together. Pressure it from every angle, and when it's gone the e5 pawn is weak.

chapters.title: King's Indian Attack and early deviations
chapters.intro: Some White players avoid d4 altogether with d3, Nd2, g3 and Bg2. Grab the centre with ...c5 and ...Nc6 and expand on the queenside with ...b5.

courses.name: French Defence
courses.tagline: Counterpunch from a solid shell: ...e6, ...d5, then hit the chain with ...c5.
courses.description: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5. You let White build a big centre and then attack its base with ...c5 and ...f6. This course covers the Advance, the Exchange, the Tarrasch, the Classical 3.Nc3 Nf6 with both 4.e5 and 4.Bg5, and the King's Indian Attack.

chapters.title: 3.Nc3 Qa5: the main line
chapters.intro: After 3.Nc3 the queen goes to a5, where it pins the c3 knight and stays safe from attacks. Then you develop with ...Nf6, ...c6 and ...Bf5, with ...e6 later. Your c6 pawn gives the queen a way back to c7 and b6.

chapters.title: White's third-move alternatives
chapters.intro: White doesn't have to play 3.Nc3. Against 3.Nf3 your bishop pins with ...Bg4. Against 3.d4 you can punish the queen's position at once with ...e5.

The Bogoljubov setup: the bishop goes to g7 to guard your king and hit d4. White's attack has nothing to bite on.

quizzes.question: White kicked your queen with 3.Nc3. Why put it on a5?
quizzes.answer: It pins the c3 knight against the king and is hard to attack there
quizzes.explanation: On a5 the queen pins the knight, can't easily be hit by minor pieces, and can drop back to c7 or d8 after ...c6.

wrong: To prepare ...b5 and attack the bishop
quizzes.question: Why play ...c6 before developing the bishop to g4?
quizzes.answer: After ...Bg4? h3 Bh5 g4 Bg6 Ne5, White's knight and bishop gang up on f7
quizzes.explanation: With White's bishop on c4, ...Bg4 can backfire badly. ...c6 first gives your queen a retreat and you can choose ...Bf5 calmly.

quizzes.question: White played 3.d4 without developing. What's the strongest answer?
quizzes.answer: 3...e5: open the centre while your queen is active
quizzes.explanation: 3...e5 4.dxe5 Qxd1+ 5.Kxd1 leaves White's king stuck in the middle, and Black wins the e5 pawn back with excellent development.

chapters.title: Early deviations: 2.Nc3 and 2.e5
chapters.intro: Some White players don't take on d5. Against 2.e5 you play a Caro-Kann-style Advance with ...Bf5. Against 2.Nc3 you can push ...d4 and grab space.

courses.name: Scandinavian Defence
courses.tagline: Hit e4 on move one and play your own game from the very start.
courses.description: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5. You trade off White's e-pawn at once and develop around the queen: ...Qa5, ...Nf6, ...c6, ...Bf5 and ...e6. The structure is like a Caro-Kann, but White has to face it on your terms. This course covers 3.Nc3 with all of White's main setups, 3.Nf3, 3.d4 and the early deviations 2.Nc3 and 2.e5, plus the traps to avoid.
